description:
EVEN MORE MADNESS!

Anáhuac Querétaro representative team at robotics and technology competitions.
summary: Delta Madness (DeltasMadness2 / sar-Madness) is an all-weather multi-sensor geospatial satellite monitoring platform that integrates SAR, optical, thermal, and digital elevation model (DEM) observations using deterministic physical models for Before and After analysis. Using official NASA pre-launch simulated NISAR L2 GCOV datasets, MODIS, Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Copernicus DEM, our platform unifies three Python scientific engines and an interactive 3D web viewer across six validated study cases. This tool empowers researchers, emergency responders, and environmental planners to visualize aboveground forest biomass and carbon loss in Alabama, wildfire burn severity and uncertainty across the United States, and glacier melt with subsurface wet snow in Nepal. Delta Madness addresses a major remote sensing challenge: traditional environmental monitoring relies heavily on clear-sky optical imagery, whereas our multi-sensor fusion with polarimetric SAR fallback reliably detects surface disturbances beneath clouds, smoke, or snow cover.
details:
Delta Madness unifies specialized Python scientific engines (biomasa, incendios, and hola) with an interactive web viewer (sar-Madness) designed to monitor critical environmental changes without relying solely on clear-sky optical imagery. All components publish standardized products under schemaVersion 2 with strictly validated real-observation provenance before rendering or building.

How it works: The platform processes satellite observations through deterministic physical pipelines: the forest biomass engine (nisar-biomass-monitor) inverts the semi-empirical NISAR L3 AGB ATBD model on simulated NISAR L2 GCOV scenes (aggregated from 20 m to 1 ha) to estimate aboveground biomass, carbon density, and severe forest loss. The wildfire engine (wildfire-monitor) fuses optical spectral indices (dNBR, NDVI, MNDWI) with an all-weather polarimetric SAR fallback (Sentinel-1 RTC VH backscatter drop where optical pixels are obscured), Copernicus DEM terrain slope, Key and Benson severity classes, a pre-event physical water mask, and Shannon binary-entropy uncertainty. Meanwhile, the glacier and alpine hydrology engine (glacier-monitor) generates multi-source compositions in Google Earth Engine (Sentinel-2 NDSI, Sentinel-1 VV/VH, and MODIS snow cover and land surface temperature) alongside connectivity to NASA ASF Search and HyP3.

Key Benefits & Impact:

  • Quantifies forest aboveground biomass and carbon loss via L-band SAR inversion.
  • Detects wildfire burn perimeters under smoke or cloud cover using polarimetric SAR fallback.
  • Monitors active wildfire alerts via NASA EONET, GDACS, and Copernicus EMS feeds.
  • Maps glacier snow loss and subsurface wet snow by combining optical, thermal, and radar sensors.
  • Provides a validated catalog of real satellite observations across biomass, wildfire, and cryosphere domains.
  • Improve preparedness for different disasters

Tools & Technologies:

  • Mapbox GL JS v3.9.0 and Vite v5.4.11: web globe viewer, terrain rendering, and swipe comparison.
  • Python 3.11+ (NumPy, SciPy, pytest): vectorized scientific engines, GeoTIFF codec, and unit testing.
  • Google Earth Engine and NASA ASF Search / HyP3: cloud geospatial processing and SAR ingestion.
  • Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC and TiTiler: optical, radar, and elevation scene querying.
  • Node.js validation scripts: automated catalog schema verification and front-end testing.

Creative Elements:

  • Interactive Globe, Flat Map, and Terrain modes with automatic open-basemap fallback.
  • Before and After geographic swipe comparison with real per-pixel cursor readout and client-side LUT colorization.
  • Multi-frame timestamp stepping across real observation dates without artificial cross-date interpolation.
  • Direct export of side-by-side comparative PNG plates and raw GeoTIFF rasters.
  • Integrated search bar for jumping to study sites, parsing WGS84 coordinates, and generating ready-to-run CLI commands.
